topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of complement complexity
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture by introducing complement as a complex yet essential immunological system.

topics.label: Foundations and core principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the overarching functions, naming conventions, and central role of C3 in complement activation.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the three recognition pathways that generate convertases and trigger complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the downstream immune functions executed once complement is activated, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details how deficiencies in specific complement proteins and regulators cause distinct clinical diseases.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement and applications
topics.groupedBecause: It explains how pathogens evade complement attack and how these mechanisms are applied in biotechnology.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
